gpu_batch_mixing.direct_record: NONE - per-batch domain composition was never logged; explicitly unanswerable at batch granularity
gpu_batch_mixing.analytic_inference: concurrency=256 in-flight requests -> each boundary produces one ~256-request (~10-12 s) two-domain transition zone; within segments forwards pack same-domain requests (chunked prefill: ~16 prover reqs or ~4 code reqs per 8192-token forward). Client-side domain switches (3) therefore equal GPU-workload transitions (3 short zones), NOT high-frequency switching.

distribution_probes.cos_sim_semantics: cosine between consecutive-window RAW all-reduced logical load vectors (per-layer, averaged); placement-independent; alpha-independent; logged by DP0 every 4th window only
distribution_probes.A00_clean_probe: all cos >= 0.9551 across 5 starts (segment means 0.9648-0.9946) -> within-segment distribution near-stationary at 16-forward granularity
distribution_probes.sampling_caveat: every-4th-window logging can miss a one-window step at a boundary (A00 boundary windows ~w#10.5/18.6/34.4 were not logged); boundary steps are instead evidenced by the D arms' ratio detectors which see every window
distribution_probes.boundary_evidence: A01: 4 resets/start in frac 0.17-0.23 right after boundary1 in 5/5 starts (deltas 0.15/0.465/0.057/0.051); A11: resets at all three boundaries in most starts (frac 0.157-0.22, 0.28-0.30, 0.51-0.55) plus mid-segment extra; P11 similar to A11
distribution_probes.per_domain_histograms: NEVER recorded anywhere (grep over results: none); all 18 prediction_v1 real captures come from the SINGLE-domain dataset L512_O1_realprover_n8192.jsonl -> per-domain normalized distributions cannot be shown

w_reset_attribution.exogenous_part: A01 first reset per start locks to boundary1 across all 5 starts with large delta (0.15-0.48) - genuine domain-shift detection; A11/P11 boundary2/boundary3 resets likewise
w_reset_attribution.noise_part: A01 subsequent resets delta only 0.05-0.07 (just above the 0.03 threshold) clustered in the prover segment = short-prompt sampling noise re-fires; A10 (W-only): ~16 shrink + 11 grow events per start spread over ALL segments, largest ratio jumps (mean 0.27, max 0.49) inside prover, not at boundaries; A10 cos drops to 0.58-0.88 in prover while A00 (same alpha=0, fixed W=16) stays >=0.958 -> the drop is self-induced by window shrink (8-forward windows halve tokens/window), i.e. endogenous churn, not exogenous change
w_reset_attribution.conclusion: W changes mainly reflect noise amplification + window-length self-feedback in the short-prompt segment; resets partially track the 3 real domain boundaries but re-fire on noise; A11 carries 3-5 extra mid-segment resets per start vs A01

break_even_estimate.assumptions: MoE layer replay ~1450 us/layer/forward x 94 layers ~ 136 ms/forward; full service ~350 ms/forward (370 s / ~1050 forwards) -> expert-execution share ~39%; oracle gap g = fraction of layer-forward time that per-domain switching recovers over the best common static layout (K-weighted)
break_even_estimate.formula: ideal service-level gain ~ 0.39 * g * 370 s, before capture-rate discount and transition costs

scenarios.g=2%: ~2.9 s - still below measured adaptivity cost
scenarios.g=5%: ~7.2 s - break-even only if the controller captures most of it AND churn is tamed to near the 3 real switches

break_even_estimate.conclusion: cross-domain g is UNKNOWN and is the single missing fact; with only 3 switches/run and measured within-domain g=0.17%, the prior is unfavorable but not decisive -> measure g offline-cheap first (Phase A), do NOT jump to service-level experiments
